I did not run any experiments or look at data. These 10 hypotheses come from reasoning about how Adam behaves in a ReLU MLP trained for a fixed 243 epochs.

- **Learning rate:** at low values the network is under-trained, so raising it helps. At high values (0.278 and 1) training diverges, so raising it hurts.
- **Batch size:** larger batches mean fewer updates per epoch. That hurts when the learning rate is low and is neutral or helpful when it is high, because larger batches reduce gradient noise.
- **Capacity:** wider and deeper networks are more unstable at high learning rates.
- **Alpha:** at the top of the grid (0.129 and 1) the L2 penalty causes underfitting, so raising it further hurts.
